A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FlyPrompt work. All 34 pages in each version, including Appendices A-G, are available and readable; text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable assessment.

before.justification: v1 reports original FlyPrompt experiments on CIFAR-100, ImageNet-R, and CUB-200, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, and supplementary analyses in Section 4 and Appendices D and F.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including Tables 1-19 and the empirical figures. Results retained from v1 still qualify as original empirical work.

M1.justification: The REAR router, temporal-ensemble experts, prompt initialization, losses, masking, and inference procedure remain unchanged in Section 3 and Algorithm 1. The added EMA citations do not change the method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three image-classification datasets under Si-Blurry, including the retained purely blurry and fully disjoint online class-incremental scenarios in Appendix F.1. No data or task coverage changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the main and appendix experiments, including prompt methods, MVP, MISA, adapted offline methods, RanPAC variants, and alternative routers. The newly cited Sun et al. works are not added experimental baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendices C-F retain the same backbones, stream configurations, training budgets, preprocessing, and evaluation procedures. Defaults remain five sessions, 50% disjoint classes, 10% blurry samples, and the same accuracy and forgetting metrics.

E4.justification: The component ablations, task-boundary analysis, CKA comparisons, masking tests, routing alternatives, and projection/EMA/aggregation sensitivity analyses are unchanged in Section 4.2 and Appendices D and F.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over five runs and disclose seeds 1-5 in Appendix C.1. No repeated-run information or uncertainty-reporting procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical tables and empirical plots are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains FlyPrompt's Sup-21K CIFAR-100 anytime accuracy of 83.24 ± 2.23% and final accuracy of 86.76 ± 0.73% under identical settings.

T1.justification: The REAR and temporal-ensemble theorems, assumptions, lemmas, and proofs in Appendix E are identical. The mathematical definitions and derivations elsewhere are also retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same expert-routing/expert-competence decomposition, biological motivation, theoretical contributions, and performance claims. No contribution is added, strengthened, or narrowed.

C2.justification: Interpretations of routing, expert specialization, ensemble behavior, and task-boundary independence remain unchanged. The conclusion retains the limitations concerning fixed EMA decay rates and extreme long-tailed distributions.

D1.justification: Implementation and baseline-adaptation details in Appendix C, pseudocode in Appendix G, and resource information are unchanged despite repagination. Hyperparameters, hardware, and the FlyGCL code-access link and release statements remain the same.

R1.justification: v3 adds Sun et al. (2025a, 2025b), two spacing-effect works, beside the naive EMA discussion in Section 3.2, and Sun et al. (2026), Mepo, in Appendix B's GCL discussion. These are limited citation additions without substantive repositioning.

P1.justification: Appendix B changes 'sequential tasks with evolving data distributions' to 'task streams with evolving distributions.' The acknowledgment revises a funding-program name, and the arXiv stamp is updated. The narrative and section order remain intact.

P2.justification: Bibliography additions change spacing and page breaks across the references and Appendices A-C, including consolidating Appendix C.2 onto one page. Figures, tables, captions, and scientific displays remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 provides small bibliographic and editorial updates without adding substantive discussion. The method, experimental evidence, proofs, reproducibility information, and limitations remain unchanged, while the limited wording and pagination edits do not materially affect clarity. Overall paper quality is effectively unchanged.
